report.summary: Payment-service write failures began at about 12:00Z and are attributed to payments-db running out of disk space, with ENOSPC errors on the INSERT path; the system determination is conclusive at confidence 0.70. payments-db logged WAL archive failures from 11:00Z and its first ENOSPC error at 11:59:29Z, about 52 seconds before the first payment-service error at 12:00:21Z, while payment-service and payments-db CPU, memory, latency, connections and request rate stayed flat. Checkout errors (about 13%) are consistent with downstream propagation through its sync call to payment-service, but its own ERROR logs are absent and clock alignment is unverified. Two unresolved issues limit certainty: disk_used_pct already read above 100% at 11:50 and 11:55 while payment errors were at baseline, so the exact 12:00 trigger is unexplained and the >100% readings are unverified. The v3.1.4 logging deploy at 09:55Z was not ruled out but has weak support.

root_cause.mechanism: payments-db data volume filled up: WAL archiving failed repeatedly from 11:00Z so WAL segments accumulated, disk_used_pct climbed from 87.84% to about 100% by 11:50Z, and INSERTs into payments fail with 'could not extend file: No space left on device'. payment-service surfaces this as about 28-32% write errors and checkout sees about 13% through its sync call to payment-service.
assumptions: The payments-db ENOSPC errors are the origin of the payment INSERT failures, not a secondary symptom.
The disk_used_pct values above 100% reflect real conditions or a reporting artifact that does not change the ordering.
The 12:00 step reflects a threshold or allocation event on top of pre-existing disk pressure, which is not directly observed.

brief.alert: ALERT [P1] payment-service error rate 30% since ~12:00 UTC. payment-service was deployed earlier today.

Symptoms are payment write failures.

Downstream dependency failure (database, ledger or payment provider) that payment-service writes depend on, possibly exposed by the deploy
Config or feature-flag change coinciding with the deploy or near 12:00 UTC that alters write path behaviour
Infrastructure or capacity event (connection pool exhaustion, timeouts) affecting payment writes and propagating to checkout-service

payment-service logged 35 ERROR lines, all 'INSERT INTO payments failed: could not extend file: No space left on device (SQLSTATE 53100)'. The first is at 12:00:21Z (L0193), and they recur roughly every 0.5-2 minutes through 12:30:00Z (L0330).

No payment-service ERROR lines appear before 12:00:21Z in the 11:00-12:30 window. The only earlier WARN is 'payment-provider responded in 1123ms' at 11:21:54Z (L0070), and a later one at 12:12:49Z (L0249, 610ms).

checkout-service's only error-related WARN in the window is 'retrying idempotent call to payment-service (attempt 2)'. It appears at 11:22:30Z (L0075, isolated, before the spike) and at 12:00:08Z (L0192), about 13 seconds before the first payment-service DB error at 12:00:21Z.

checkout-service logged only 4 WARN lines in the window: two 'slow inventory reservation' (1148ms at 11:01:02Z, 1293ms at 12:21:50Z) and the two retry warnings. It has no ERROR lines in the window, even though its error_rate is about 13%.

Payment-service resource metrics show no comparable change at 12:00. cpu_pct stayed 31.7-34.3%, memory_pct 52.8-56.8% (max at 12:00 bucket, 56.84%, similar to earlier), latency_p99_ms 436-468ms, and request_rate 57.7-62.2 req/s with no drop. The pattern matches a write-path failure, not overload.
Checkout-service resource metrics stayed normal across 12:00: cpu_pct 39.9-42.6%, memory_pct 55.7-59.7%, latency_p99_ms 308-332ms, request_rate 81.7-87.5 req/s.

Payment-service's error volume is 'could not extend file' from the DB write, and its error rate (~28-32%) is larger than checkout's (~13%), consistent with checkout only seeing a fraction of its calls fail after retries.

interpretations.statement: The payment write failures start at 12:00 UTC and are caused by the database running out of disk space (could not extend file / ENOSPC on the payments insert path). Checkout's elevated errors are downstream of payment-service failures.

The deployment is not confirmed as the trigger from telemetry alone. The onset is at 12:00 UTC and the failure is a storage error, not a code error, so the deploy may only be coincident, or it may have changed write volume or logging. This needs the deploy timestamp and the DB disk-usage trend.

The checkout retry warning at 12:00:08Z, 13 seconds before the first payment DB error at 12:00:21Z, may reflect sampling or clock skew between the services rather than a true ordering. Under either reading, checkout errors begin within the same minute as payment errors.

critique.summary: The storage-exhaustion hypothesis (H1) is the best supported: payments-db logs ENOSPC errors and payment-service INSERT failures carry the same message, and payment-service resource metrics are flat. Two points are not resolved. First, disk_used_pct was already at or above 100% at 11:50 and 11:55 while payment errors stayed at baseline, and the database's first ENOSPC ERROR is at 11:59:29, so the disk metric and the onset need reconciling. Second, checkout's retry warning at 12:00:08 precedes the first payment ERROR at 12:00:21, which the analysis treats as clock skew without verifying it. The 15 unread payments-db WARN/ERROR lines and the v3.1.4 logging-volume question are also open. Confidence of 0.80 is somewhat high given these gaps.

issues.detail: disk_used_pct is reported at 100.88% at 11:50 and 100.77% at 11:55 with payment errors at baseline. The analysis attributes this to an unexplained threshold, but it does not test whether the disk metric is accurate, and values above 100% suggest a metric artifact. If the disk reading is wrong, the storage cause and its timing are both in doubt.

Checkout's attempt-2 retry at 12:00:08Z precedes the first payment-service ERROR at 12:00:21Z. This could indicate a failure on the checkout-to-payment path before the database error is logged, or a timing alignment issue. The analysis dismisses this as skew without checking clocks or the checkout call trace.

Only 20 of 35 payments-db WARN/ERROR lines were read. The remaining 15 may include the WAL archive failure sequence and the disk allocation events near 11:55-12:00 that decide whether storage or WAL growth is the trigger. These can be retrieved with the existing tools.

The deploy is ranked low on the basis of a logging-only description. The v3.1.4 log volume and any change in payment-service write rate were never measured, so the deploy-as-accelerant mechanism is untested rather than refuted.

Confidence of 0.80 relies on log ordering (database ENOSPC 52 seconds before the first payment error) while the 11:50 disk reading and the 12:00 trigger remain unexplained, and no disk history before 11:00 is available to test whether pre-existing pressure caused the failure.

analysis.response_to_critique: 1. The >100% disk reading at 11:50 and 11:55 with baseline payment errors: accepted as unresolved. Confidence is lowered to 0.70 and the reasoning states that the trigger is not explained and the metric may be an artifact; the filesystem free-space check remains needed. 2. Checkout retry preceding the payment error by 13 seconds: accepted as unverified. Clock alignment and call traces are listed as needed; the retry is not used as evidence for ordering. 3. The 15 unread payments-db lines: the T5 retrieval found the WAL archive failures from 11:00Z and ENOSPC errors from 11:59:29Z, and no allocation or autogrow events between 11:50 and 12:00Z, so the critique's concern is partly addressed, with the remaining gap noted. 4. H2 deploy ranking: accepted that it is untested rather than refuted; it is kept at 0.20 and the log-volume measurement is listed as needed. 5. H1 overconfidence: accepted and reduced from 0.80 to 0.70.

critique.summary: The leading hypothesis H1 (payments-db storage exhaustion producing ENOSPC on the payment insert path) is well supported by the ledger: payments-db logs ENOSPC at 11:59:29Z before the first payment ERROR at 12:00:21Z, WAL archive failures begin at 11:00:11Z, and payment resource metrics are flat. However, the analysis overstates certainty in places. disk_used_pct was above 100% at 11:50 and 11:55 while payment error rate stayed at baseline, which the analysis acknowledges but does not reconcile with a full-disk cause for the 12:00 onset. The >100% readings are unverified and the 12:00 trigger is unexplained. Checkout's retry precedes the first payment error by 13 seconds with unverified clock alignment, and checkout has no ERROR lines despite ~13% errors. The analysis also states the cause of checkout errors as settled when only propagation is inferred. No further investigation rounds remain, so the conclusion should be revised to reflect these limits rather than requesting more data.

issues.detail: The analysis cites disk_used_pct as a clean fill-to-100% trajectory, but values of 100.88%, 100.77% and 103.97% exceed a physical maximum; the reading is unverified and the claim that the disk is genuinely full rests on a metric that may be an artifact. Confidence should reflect that.

Disk was at 100.88% at 11:50 and 100.77% at 11:55 while payment error rate stayed at 0.15-0.25%, and the first ENOSPC error came only at 11:59:29Z. If a full disk were sufficient, payment errors would have started earlier. The exact 12:00 trigger (allocation event, threshold, or different write path) is not identified, so H1's mechanism for timing is incomplete even though the ordering is consistent.
The deploy v3.1.4 (C09) is dismissed on a 2-hour gap and logging-only content, but no log volume or write-path diff was measured, so a contribution to disk growth is not ruled out by the ledger.

H2 is kept at 0.20 with supporting evidence C09 and M39, but M39 shows disk growth from 11:00 onward only, and no pre-deploy slope exists, so the deploy-as-accelerator mechanism is speculative. Its confidence is appropriate but its support is thin.

H3 lists M41 as both supporting and contradicting. M41 (replication lag normal) does not support an archive-pipeline root cause; it only rules out replication as the cause of archive failure. The support is weak and the entry should not count as support.

Checkout is described as downstream of payment-service errors, but checkout's attempt-2 retry at 12:00:08Z is not linked to any payment error response, and checkout has no ERROR lines. The causal direction is inferred from the sync_http edge only.

reasons: confidence 0.70, margin 0.50, 10 verified supporting and 5 contradicting evidence items (33%)
